verdict.rationale: RudderStack's own docs describe an open-source version that runs as a standalone system needing only PostgreSQL, with data-plane and control-plane components, so self-hosting the core event pipeline is a first-party capability. The evidence does not show how much of the full product the self-hosted edition includes or how to deploy it, so coverage is partial. Community notes about the license moving from AGPLv3 to Elastic do not contradict that self-hosting is possible. Missing for 10: deployment or installation documentation (Docker/Kubernetes guides), clarity on which features (Profiles, Audiences, MCP, AI features) are available when self-hosted, and independent hands-on corroboration of running a self-hosted instance.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: The open source version of RudderStack is a standalone system dependent only on a database (PostgreSQL). It consists of 2 major components: data plane and control plane
